children: Shares of Britannia Industries were trading sharply higher on Wednesday afternoon, rising ₹75.60 or 1.58 per cent to ₹4,865.60 on the NSE by 1.03 PM, a reaction to the company’s second-quarter results. The stock, part of the Nifty Next 50, touched an intraday high of ₹4,874 against a previous close of ₹4,790.

Trading activity was notable, with 1.61 lakh shares changing hands for a value of ₹78.29 crore. Buy orders accounted for 47.13 per cent of total market depth versus 52.87 per cent on the sell side, suggesting buyers were driving the move despite lingering caution. Deliverable trades stood at 56.41 per cent of total volume, indicating some conviction behind the uptick.

Axis Direct, which published its result update on Monday, maintained a Buy rating but cut its target price to ₹5,575 from ₹6,590, implying a 16 per cent upside from the current market price. The brokerage also trimmed its FY27 and FY28 EBITDA and PAT estimates by 7–8 per cent, citing elevated input costs and geopolitical pressures stemming from the West Asia conflict.

UBS echoed a Buy stance with a higher target of ₹5,800. The foreign brokerage noted the stock had corrected roughly 20 per cent year-to-date on inflation concerns and now trades at a 12-month forward P/E of approximately 39x, about 15 per cent below its five-year median, making valuations more attractive. However, UBS flagged that a meaningful margin recovery has been deferred to FY28.

The trigger for today’s move was Britannia’s Q2FY27 numbers: revenue rose 16.6 per cent year-on-year to ₹5,542 crore on the back of 13 per cent volume growth. Net profit grew 10.2 per cent to ₹721 crore. The beat on the top line offset a margin miss, with EBITDA margin contracting 147 basis points to 18.3 per cent due to surging palm oil, industrial fuel, and sugar costs.
The stock remains down over 18 per cent in the past year against the Nifty Next 50’s 5.39 per cent gain over the same period, with its 52-week high of ₹6,271 hit as recently as January 7 this year.

title: Britannia shares climb 1.6% mid-session as Q2 results digest
